page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory. It is equipped with 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3080.18 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2103.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Text processing is also strong at 2572.0. Multi-core and general compute metrics fall into the average range, including a Passmark CPU score of 7564.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4846.0. However, memory read bandwidth is weak, measuring 303.4 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 37.16 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also in the lower 25% tier, with Redis achieving 5.91 million operations per second.

The E4ads_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing or high-throughput memory reads. While single-threaded tasks and basic web serving perform adequately, the instance exhibits limitations in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and medium-sized LLM inference. It is best suited for memory-optimized applications, caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring local NVMe storage.
